product.title: NOLITA Frog Skin Camo Overshirt
product.body_html:
24 hours Pre-order // Expected shipping date November 2026

The NOLITA Frog Skin Camo Overshirt is our Brooklyn take on a piece of military history. Frog skin — the iconic WWII-era camouflage pattern worn by the first Marine Raiders — gets reinterpreted here in a 10oz Japanese back satin: a tightly woven 100% cotton fabric with a smooth face, subtle sheen, and the kind of structured hand that softens beautifully with wear.

Designed to wear open as a light layer or buttoned as a standalone piece. Triple-stitched seams, hidden interior pockets, and outside hand-warming pockets built for real use. Every snap is pure brass, milled in Connecticut.

Made in Williamsburg, Brooklyn.

In 1942, a garden editor at Better Homes and Gardens designed the first camouflage pattern in American military history. Norvell Gillespie, a horticulturist by training, looked to nature — the mottled skin of a frog, the way light breaks through a forest canopy — and created a five-color disruptive pattern that would become known as frog skin.

The Marine Raiders wore it first, landing on Tulagi in the Solomon Islands in the dark early hours of August 6, 1942. It went on to see action at Guadalcanal and Bougainville, briefly appeared at Normandy before being pulled back — it looked too much like SS camouflage and was causing friendly fire — and eventually made its way into surplus stores, then hunting gear, then street culture. The CIA issued it to Cuban exiles for the Bay of Pigs. Special Forces gave it to the Montagnard in Vietnam. It's one of the most traveled patterns in the history of American cloth.

product.title: NAVY YARD Sashiko Chore Coat
product.body_html:
Note: Indigo transfer can occur with sashiko fabric and will decrease and stop with wear. Avoid white surfaces while breaking in. 

The NAVY YARD Sashiko Chore Coat is our Brooklyn take on one of the oldest garments in the working world. It combines two of our all time favorite things: sashiko fabric — a Japanese stitching technique that became a fabric, dating back centuries — meets the chore coat, a silhouette born in 19th century France and worn by laborers on both sides of the Atlantic ever since.

The result is a 16oz coat built to last decades, rinsed once to remove shrinkage but preserves the deep indigo color that will fade beautifully with time and wear. Real horn buttons. Triple-stitched seams. Hidden interior pockets. Made at 108 Bayard Street, Williamsburg, Brooklyn — a couple miles from the Navy Yard.

The chore coat begins in France, around 1844. A garment for railway workers, farmers, and factory laborers — built from cotton drill or moleskin, dyed with a benzoate-based blue that would hide the stains of manual labor. They called it the bleu de travail. "Blue work." The term "blue collar" follows from the same cloth.

By the 1920s, Carhartt had brought it to America with triple-stitched seams, riveted pockets, and a corduroy collar. Paul Newman wore one in Cool Hand Luke. Tupac wore one to the Soul Train Awards in 1993. Bill Cunningham rode his bike around New York City in one well into his 80s. It has appeared on the runways of Valentino, Balenciaga, and Prada without ever fundamentally changing what it is: a boxy cut, patch pockets, a button front, and cloth tough enough to outlast the person wearing it.

In Japan, a parallel tradition was developing — the noragi, a loose indigo jacket worn by farmers and artisans, reinforced with sashiko stitching to extend the life of the garment through hard use. The techniques are different. The philosophy is identical.

The OG 718 Fatigue Pant is our modern interpretation of the historic fatigue pants worn by the U.S. military from the 1950s through the 1970s, including the Korean and Vietnam War eras. We studied original references closely, then refined the design with contemporary updates that elevate both function and feel.

Constructed from a 10oz Japanese back satin fabric, this cloth features a soft yet durable structure, woven with American cotton and milled in Japan. The fabric offers a balance of comfort and resilience, designed to break in naturally over time while maintaining its integrity.

Design details include pure brass snap buttons at the waistband tabs and leg openings, along with considered pocket construction. The front andrear cargo pockets are tacked down to create clean lines while still allowing for practical storage and ease of movement.

product.title: PFT 240 LS American Cotton Tee (White)
product.body_html:
The PFT 240 LS (Long Sleeve) is made from 100% American-grown cotton by a zero waist yarn manufacturer in North Carolina. This lightweight medium weight tee is grown, woven, cut, and sewn entirely in the USA, honoring the full American-made tradition from fiber to finished garment. It's one of the most luxurious t-shirts on the market today.

FIT
We designed this tee to solve the biggest problem in men’s basics: a premium T-shirt that's soft and structured from day one, with an impeccable fit. The silhouette has a clean, tailored drape -- not boxy, never clingy -- and the sleeves don't gap out, making it a flattering staple for daily wear, layering, or dressing up.

This is a slightly more fitted cut, so we do suggest sizing up one size compared to the short sleeved PFTs.

  • Super-soft American cotton

  • Pre-softened and pre-shrunk
  • Comfortable from day one
  • Surprisingly durable

  • 20/1 compact yarn for strength and softness
  • 240 GSM / 7 oz medium-weight knit

  • Proudly woven and made in the USA
